check: verify the third transcribed line, and record the encoding trap it exposed
result: All three lines in the traversal certificate are confirmed present in build/smoke-pass.log, so the transcription is verbatim and the certificate stands alone once the log is deleted by the final clean.

theEncodingTrap.whatHappened: Reading the file's tail and decoding with UTF-8 found nothing, even though the line is there. The file is UTF-16LE, so every ASCII character carries an interleaved zero byte and the text reads as spaced-out letters.
theEncodingTrap.whyItMatters: This is the same class of error recorded earlier for this project: a search in the wrong encoding reports absence rather than reporting an error. Here it would have looked like the certificate cited a line the log does not contain.
theEncodingTrap.correctDecoding: System.Text.Encoding.Unicode, after which the pattern matches immediately
theEncodingTrap.howItWasCaught: The tail was printed as text and showed spaced characters, which is the signature of UTF-16 read as UTF-8.

methodNote.killedScan: The first attempt line-by-line scanned all 17.68 GB, which competes for disk I/O with the running stress profile. That job was killed; reading only the last 128 KB answers the same question.
methodNote.seekNotRead: Opening the file with FileShare.ReadWrite and seeking from the end avoids both the full scan and any conflict with the profile that may still hold the file.
